claim: Single cell transcriptomic atlases of vomeronasal organs (VNO) from juvenile and adult mice were generated.
source: We have generated single cell transcriptomic atlases of vomeronasal organs (VNO) from juvenile and adult mice.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that the authors generated single cell transcriptomic atlases.

claim: A distinct, previously unidentified class of cells that express the vomeronasal receptors (VRs) was uncovered.
source: Combined with spatial molecular imaging, we uncover a distinct, previously unidentified class of cells that express the vomeronasal receptors (VRs) and a population of canonical olfactory sensory neurons in the VNO.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the study combining scRNA-seq with spatial imaging.

claim: A population of canonical olfactory sensory neurons exists in the VNO.
source: Combined with spatial molecular imaging, we uncover a distinct, previously unidentified class of cells that express the vomeronasal receptors (VRs) and a population of canonical olfactory sensory neurons in the VNO.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: High-resolution trajectory and cluster analyses reveal the lineage relationship and spatial distribution of cell types in the VNO.
source: High-resolution trajectory and cluster analyses reveal the lineage relationship, spatial distribution of cell types, and a putative cascade of molecular events that specify the V1r, V2r, and OR lineages from a common stem cell population.
evidence: The abstract describes the analytical methods and their results.

claim: A putative cascade of molecular events specifies the V1r, V2r, and OR lineages from a common stem cell population.
source: High-resolution trajectory and cluster analyses reveal the lineage relationship, spatial distribution of cell types, and a putative cascade of molecular events that specify the V1r, V2r, and OR lineages from a common stem cell population.
evidence: The abstract describes this as a finding from trajectory analysis.

claim: The expression of vomeronasal and olfactory receptors follow power law distributions.
source: The expression of vomeronasal and olfactory receptors follow power law distributions, but there is high variability in average expression levels between individual receptor and cell types.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding about receptor expression patterns.

claim: There is high variability in average expression levels between individual receptor and cell types.
source: The expression of vomeronasal and olfactory receptors follow power law distributions, but there is high variability in average expression levels between individual receptor and cell types.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this observation about expression variability.

claim: Substantial co-expression is found between receptors across clades, from different classes, and between olfactory and VRs.
source: Substantial co-expression is found between receptors across clades, from different classes, and between olfactory and VRs, with nearly half from pairs located on the same chromosome.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes this finding about receptor co-expression.

claim: Nearly half of co-expressed receptor pairs are located on the same chromosome.
source: Substantial co-expression is found between receptors across clades, from different classes, and between olfactory and VRs, with nearly half from pairs located on the same chromosome.
evidence: The abstract provides this quantitative finding about chromosomal location of co-expressed receptors.

claim: The expression of V2r, but not V1r, genes is associated with various transcription factors.
source: Interestingly, the expression of V2r, but not V1r, genes is associated with various transcription factors, suggesting distinct mechanisms of receptor choice associated with the two cell types.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this differential association with transcription factors.

claim: Distinct mechanisms of receptor choice are associated with V1r and V2r cell types.
source: Interestingly, the expression of V2r, but not V1r, genes is associated with various transcription factors, suggesting distinct mechanisms of receptor choice associated with the two cell types.
evidence: The abstract suggests this interpretation based on the differential transcription factor associations.

claim: Association between transcription factors, surface axon guidance molecules, and individual VRs was identified.
source: We identify association between transcription factors, surface axon guidance molecules, and individual VRs, thereby uncovering a molecular code that guides the specification of the vomeronasal circuitry.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: A molecular code guides the specification of the vomeronasal circuitry.
source: We identify association between transcription factors, surface axon guidance molecules, and individual VRs, thereby uncovering a molecular code that guides the specification of the vomeronasal circuitry.
evidence: The abstract presents this as an interpretation of the associations found.

claim: In many terrestrial species, the vomeronasal organ (VNO) is dedicated to the detection of inter- and intra-species chemosensory cues.
source: In many terrestrial species, the vomeronasal organ (VNO) is dedicated to the detection of inter- and intra-species chemosensory cues (Birch, 1974; Wyatt, 2003; Brennan and Zufall, 2006; Isogai et al., 2011; He et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Detection of chemosensory cues triggers innate neuroendocrine responses and elicits stereotypic social and reproductive behaviors.
source: Detection of these cues triggers innate neuroendocrine responses and elicits stereotypic social and reproductive behaviors (Birch, 1974; Wyatt, 2003; Bruce, 1969; Drickamer and Assmann, 1981; Halpern and Martínez-Marcos, 2003; Vandenbergh, 1983; Vandenbergh, 1989; Clancy et al., 1984; Maruniak et al., 1986; Meredith, 1998; Lonstein and Gammie, 2002; Ferguson et al., 2002; Dey et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by extensive citations to prior literature.

claim: The VNO shares a developmental origin with the main olfactory epithelium (MOE).
source: The VNO shares a developmental origin with the main olfactory epithelium (MOE), which detects the odor world at large and allows associative learning to take place.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Both VNO and MOE develop from the olfactory placode during early embryogenesis.
source: Both develop from the olfactory placode during early embryogenesis (Yoshida et al., 1993), but the two sensory organs follow different developmental trajectories to establish distinct characteristics in morphology, cellular composition, and molecular features.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The VNO and MOE follow different developmental trajectories to establish distinct characteristics in morphology, cellular composition, and molecular features.
source: Both develop from the olfactory placode during early embryogenesis (Yoshida et al., 1993), but the two sensory organs follow different developmental trajectories to establish distinct characteristics in morphology, cellular composition, and molecular features.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Single cell atlases of the MOE have been generated to reveal details in its molecular composition and developmental trajectories.
source: Single cell atlases of the MOE have been generated to reveal astonishing details in its molecular composition and developmental trajectories (Olender et al., 2016; Tsukahara et al., 2021; Hanchate et al., 2015; Fletcher et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Transcriptomic data of the VNO is not extensive.
source: Transcriptomic data of the VNO is not extensive (Villamayor et al., 2021; Duyck et al., 2017), but single cell analyses have already provided critical information about VNO development (Katreddi et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature with citations.

claim: Single cell analyses have provided critical information about VNO development.
source: Transcriptomic data of the VNO is not extensive (Villamayor et al., 2021; Duyck et al., 2017), but single cell analyses have already provided critical information about VNO development (Katreddi et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent single cell studies.

claim: Vomeronasal sensory neurons (VSNs) express three families of G-protein-coupled receptors: V1rs, V2rs, and formyl peptide receptors (Fprs).
source: The vomeronasal sensory neurons (VSNs) express three families of G-protein-coupled receptors, the V1rs, V2rs, and the formyl peptide receptors (Fprs) (Herrada and Dulac, 1997; Ryba and Tirindelli, 1997; Rivière et al., 2009; Liberles et al., 2009; Dulac and Axel, 1995; Matsunami and Buck, 1997; Rodriguez et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The vomeronasal receptors (VRs) comprise more than 400 members.
source: With more than 400 members, the vomeronasal receptors (VRs) are among the fastest evolving genes (Grus and Zhang, 2006; Shi and Zhang, 2007; Silva and Antunes, 2017; Lane et al., 2004; Kurzweil et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2004).
evidence: This quantitative statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The vomeronasal receptors (VRs) are among the fastest evolving genes.
source: With more than 400 members, the vomeronasal receptors (VRs) are among the fastest evolving genes (Grus and Zhang, 2006; Shi and Zhang, 2007; Silva and Antunes, 2017; Lane et al., 2004; Kurzweil et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to evolutionary studies.

claim: Signaling pathways in the VNO include the Gi2 and Go proteins.
source: Signaling pathways in the VNO include the Gi2 and Go proteins, and a combination of Trpc2, Girk1, Sk3, and Tmem16a ion channels, to transduce activation of the VRs (Liman and Corey, 1996; Yu, 2015; Wu et al., 1996; Dibattista et al., 2008; Dibattista et al., 2012; Amjad et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2010; Yang and Delay, 2010; Spehr et al., 2002; Lucas et al., 2003; Kelliher et al., 2006; Berghard and Buck, 1996; Kim et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2011; Trouillet et al., 2019; Chamero et al., 2011; Menco et al., 2001; Zufall, 2005; Stowers et al., 2002; Leypold et al., 2002; Liman and Dulac, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by extensive citations to prior literature.

claim: A combination of Trpc2, Girk1, Sk3, and Tmem16a ion channels transduce activation of the VRs.
source: Signaling pathways in the VNO include the Gi2 and Go proteins, and a combination of Trpc2, Girk1, Sk3, and Tmem16a ion channels, to transduce activation of the VRs (Liman and Corey, 1996; Yu, 2015; Wu et al., 1996; Dibattista et al., 2008; Dibattista et al., 2012; Amjad et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2010; Yang and Delay, 2010; Spehr et al., 2002; Lucas et al., 2003; Kelliher et al., 2006; Berghard and Buck, 1996; Kim et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2011; Trouillet et al., 2019; Chamero et al., 2011; Menco et al., 2001; Zufall, 2005; Stowers et al., 2002; Leypold et al., 2002; Liman and Dulac, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by extensive citations to prior literature.

claim: The spatially segregated expression of Gi2 and Go, as well as the VR genes, suggests two major classes of neurons.
source: The spatially segregated expression of Gi2 and Go, as well as the VR genes suggests two major classes of neurons.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from known expression patterns.

claim: Pheromones are highly specific in activating the VSNs.
source: Pheromones are highly specific in activating the VSNs (He et al., 2008; Leinders-Zufall et al., 2000; Haga-Yamanaka et al., 2015; He et al., 2010; Boschat et al., 2002; Holy et al., 2000; Nodari et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: VSNs residing in the apical layer of the VNO express V1R (Vmn1r) genes in a monoallelic manner.
source: Previous studies have shown that VSNs residing in the apical layer of the VNO express V1R (Vmn1r) genes in a monoallelic manner (Boschat et al., 2002; Roppolo et al., 2007; Rodriguez et al., 1999), whereas the basal VSNs express one or two of the broadly expressed C clade of V2R (Vmn2r) genes, plus a unique V2R gene belonging to another clade (Herrada and Dulac, 1997; Ryba and Tirindelli, 1997; Rivière et al., 2009; Liberles et al., 2009; Dulac and Axel, 1995; Matsunami and Buck, 1997; Martini et al., 2001; Silvotti et al., 2011; Silvotti et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Basal VSNs express one or two of the broadly expressed C clade of V2R (Vmn2r) genes, plus a unique V2R gene belonging to another clade.
source: Previous studies have shown that VSNs residing in the apical layer of the VNO express V1R (Vmn1r) genes in a monoallelic manner (Boschat et al., 2002; Roppolo et al., 2007; Rodriguez et al., 1999), whereas the basal VSNs express one or two of the broadly expressed C clade of V2R (Vmn2r) genes, plus a unique V2R gene belonging to another clade (Herrada and Dulac, 1997; Ryba and Tirindelli, 1997; Rivière et al., 2009; Liberles et al., 2009; Dulac and Axel, 1995; Matsunami and Buck, 1997; Martini et al., 2001; Silvotti et al., 2011; Silvotti et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by extensive citations to prior literature.

claim: VSNs expressing the same receptor project to dozens of glomeruli in the AOB.
source: VSNs expressing the same receptor project to dozens of glomeruli in the AOB (Rodriguez et al., 1999; Belluscio et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Individual stimuli activate broad areas in the AOB.
source: Individual stimuli activate broad areas in the AOB (Meeks et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The dendrites of the mitral cells in the AOB innervate multiple glomeruli.
source: Moreover, the dendrites of the mitral cells in the AOB innervate multiple glomeruli (Del Punta et al., 2002; Wagner et al., 2006; Takami and Graziadei, 1991).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The multi-glomerular innervation pattern in the AOB is in stark contrast with the main olfactory system, where OSNs expressing the same odorant receptor converge their axons into mostly a single glomerulus in each hemisphere of the MOB.
source: This multi-glomerular innervation pattern is in stark contrast with the main olfactory system, where OSNs expressing the same odorant receptor converge their axons into mostly a single glomerulus in each hemisphere of the main olfactory bulb (MOB; Mombaerts et al., 1996).
evidence: This comparison is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: When the convergent glomerular innervation in the MOB is experimentally perturbed to become divergent, it does not affect detection or discrimination of odorants but diminishes behavioral responses to innately recognized odors.
source: In the MOB, when the convergent glomerular innervation is experimentally perturbed to become divergent, it does not affect detection or discrimination of odorants but diminishes behavioral responses to innately recognized odors (Gronowitz et al., 2021; Qiu et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Mitral cell dendrites innervate glomeruli containing the same VR type such that the divergent projection pattern of the VSNs is rendered convergent by the mitral cells.
source: Consistent with this notion, it has been shown that mitral cell dendrites innervate glomeruli containing the same VR type such that the divergent projection pattern of the VSNs is rendered convergent by the mitral cells (Del Punta et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Heterotypic convergence, where axons expressing different receptors innervate the same glomeruli, is also observed.
source: To a lesser extent, heterotypic convergence, that is, axons expressing different receptors innervating the same glomeruli, is also observed (Wagner et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: From four adult (P56) and four juvenile (P14) mice with equal representation of sexes, sequence reads from 34,519 cells were obtained.
source: From four adult (P56) and four juvenile (P14) mice (equal representation of sexes) we obtained sequence reads from 34,519 cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental data collected.

claim: 18 cell clusters can be clearly identified in two-dimensional UMAP space.
source: In two-dimensional UMAP space, 18 cell clusters can be clearly identified (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: There was no obvious difference in the presence of cell clusters between juvenile and adult VNOs.
source: There was no obvious difference in the presence of cell clusters between juvenile and adult VNOs (Figure 1C) or between male and female sexes (Figure 1D).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: There was no obvious difference in the presence of cell clusters between male and female sexes.
source: There was no obvious difference in the presence of cell clusters between juvenile and adult VNOs (Figure 1C) or between male and female sexes (Figure 1D).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1D.

claim: There were differences in gene expression profiles between P14 and P56 ages.
source: Although there were differences in gene expression profiles between the ages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and sexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), the list of significantly differentially expressed genes did not appear to be influential for the neuronal lineage and cell type specification, or related to cell adhesion molecules, which were the main focuses of this study.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There were differences in gene expression profiles between male and female sexes.
source: Although there were differences in gene expression profiles between the ages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and sexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), the list of significantly differentially expressed genes did not appear to be influential for the neuronal lineage and cell type specification, or related to cell adhesion molecules, which were the main focuses of this study.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The list of significantly differentially expressed genes between ages and sexes did not appear to be influential for the neuronal lineage and cell type specification, or related to cell adhesion molecules.
source: Although there were differences in gene expression profiles between the ages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and sexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), the list of significantly differentially expressed genes did not appear to be influential for the neuronal lineage and cell type specification, or related to cell adhesion molecules, which were the main focuses of this study.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential expression analysis results.

claim: The largest portion of cells belonged to the neuronal lineage, including GBC, INPs, immature and mature VSNs, and a population of cells that do not co-cluster with either VSN type.
source: The largest portion of cells belonged to the neuronal lineage, including the globose basal cells (GBC), immediate neuronal progenitors (INPs), the immature and mature VSNs, and a population of cells that do not co-cluster with either VSN type (see below).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the clustering results.

claim: There were substantial numbers of sustentacular cells (SCs), horizontal basal cells (HBCs), and ms4-expressing microvillus cells (MVs).
source: There were substantial numbers of sustentacular cells (SCs), horizontal basal cells (HBCs), and ms4-expressing microvillus cells (MVs).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the cell types identified.

claim: Cells engaged in adaptive immune responses, including microglia and T-cells, were detected.
source: Cells engaged in adaptive immune responses, including microglia and T-cells, were also detected.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the cell types identified.

claim: A population of Fpr-1 expressing cells that were distinctive from the VSNs expressing the Fpr family of genes formed a separate class.
source: A population of Fpr-1 expressing cells that were distinctive from the VSNs expressing the Fpr family of genes formed a separate class.
evidence: This is a direct statement about a distinct cell population identified.

claim: Fpr-1 expressing cells were likely resident cells mediating innate immune responses.
source: These were likely resident cells mediating innate immune responses.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the identity of the Fpr-1 expressing cells.

claim: Olfactory ensheathing cells (OECs) were identified.
source: We also identified the olfactory ensheathing cells (OECs) and a population of lamina propria (LP) cells, which share molecular characteristics with what we have found in the MOE (Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a direct statement about cell types identified.

claim: A population of lamina propria (LP) cells was identified, which share molecular characteristics with what was found in the MOE.
source: We also identified the olfactory ensheathing cells (OECs) and a population of lamina propria (LP) cells, which share molecular characteristics with what we have found in the MOE (Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a direct statement about cell types identified with comparison to prior work.

claim: 100 target genes were selected based on the scRNA-seq results for spatial molecular imaging.
source: To obtain the spatial location of the various cell types, we selected 100 target genes based on the scRNA-seq results.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental approach.

claim: The VSNs and supporting cells are located in the pseudostratified neuroepithelium.
source: This analysis revealed that the VSNs and supporting cells are located in the pseudostratified neuroepithelium (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: LP cells are located along the LP underlying the neuroepithelium as found in the MOE.
source: The LP cells are located along the LP underlying the neuroepithelium as found in the MOE (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 1F and G.

claim: There are few HBCs located along the basal lamina, in direct contrast to the MOE.
source: Surprisingly, however, there are few HBCs located along the basal lamina, in direct contrast to the MOE (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 1F and G.

claim: Most of the HBCs are found in the non-neuronal epithelium surrounding the blood vessel, with few near the marginal zone.
source: Most of the HBCs are found in the non-neuronal epithelium surrounding the blood vessel, with few near the marginal zone.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the spatial distribution of HBCs.

claim: The marginal zone is thought to be the neurogenic region.
source: The marginal zone is thought to be the neurogenic region (Takami and Graziadei, 1991; Mombaerts et al., 1996; Gronowitz et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: There are significantly more GBCs, INPs, and immature VSNs in the marginal zone than in the main zone.
source: We quantified the distribution of cell types in various regions of the VNO neuroepithelia (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A) and found significantly more GBCs, INPs, and immature VSNs in the marginal zone than in the main zone (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B and Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B and C.

claim: A previous study suggested neurogenic activity in the medial zone, but the current study did not find evidence in support of that conclusion.
source: A previous study suggested neurogenic activity in the medial zone (Brann and Firestein, 2010), but we did not find evidence in support of that conclusion, which was largely based on BrdU staining of mitotic cells without lineage-specific information.
evidence: This is a direct statement comparing the current findings to prior work.

claim: Neurogenic activity is restricted to the marginal zone.
source: Based on our transcriptomic analysis, we conclude that neurogenic activity is restricted to the marginal zone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Cells expressing Xist, which is expressed in female cells, were intermingled with those from males.
source: Cells expressing Xist, which is expressed in female cells, were intermingled with those from males (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The cell types are not sexually dimorphic.
source: This observation is consistent with our previous studies using bulk sequencing indicating that the cell types are not sexually dimorphic (Duyck et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as consistent with prior work by the authors.

claim: The VSNs are clearly separated into the V1R and V2R clusters as distinguished by the expression of Gnai2 and Gnao1, respectively.
source: The VSNs are clearly separated into the V1R and V2R clusters as distinguished by the expression of Gnai2 and Gnao1, respectively (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A portion of the V2R cells also expressed Gnai2, primarily from adult male mice.
source: Surprisingly, we observed that a portion of the V2R cells also expressed Gnai2. These cells were primarily from adult, but not juvenile male mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A major group of cells expressed the prototypical VSN markers but formed a cluster distinct from the mature V1R and V2R cells.
source: We found a major group of cells that expressed the prototypical VSN markers but formed a cluster distinct from the mature V1R and V2R cells (Figures 1A and 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 1A and 2A.

claim: The distinct cluster of cells expressed fewer overall genes and with lower total counts when compared with the mature V1R and V2R cells.
source: These cells expressed fewer overall genes and with lower total counts when compared with the mature V1R and V2R cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: The lower ribosomal gene expression in the distinct cluster suggests that these neurons are less active in protein translation.
source: The lower ribosomal gene expression suggests that these neurons are less active in protein translation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ribosomal gene expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: There are 503 differentially expressed genes in the distinct cluster when compared with other mature neurons (padj <0.001; FC >1.5).
source: There are 503 differentially expressed genes in this cluster when compared with other mature neurons (padj <0.001; FC >1.5; Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about differential expression analysis shown in figures.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) analysis reveals that differentially expressed genes enriched in the distinct cluster are associated with odorant binding proteins.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis reveals that differentially expressed genes enriched in this group are associated with odorant binding proteins (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Mucin 2 (Muc2), odorant binding protein 2 a (Obp2a), Obp2b, and lipocalin 3 (Lcn3) genes are expressed at higher levels in the distinct cluster neurons than the canonical VSNs.
source: Correspondingly, mucin 2 (Muc2), odorant binding protein 2 a (Obp2a), Obp2b, and lipocalin 3 (Lcn3) genes, usually enriched in non-neuronal supporting or secretory gland cells, are expressed at higher levels in these neurons than the canonical VSNs (Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: The distinct cluster cells have higher expression of Wnk1, Neat1, P2ry14, Zfp738, and Cspp1.
source: They also have higher expression of Wnk1, which is involved in ion transport, the lncRNA Neat1, the purinergic receptor P2ry14, the zinc finger protein Zfp738, and the centrosome and spindle pole associated Cspp1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E–I).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E–I.

claim: The distinct cluster cells exhibit lower expression of Omp and JunD.
source: On the other hand, these cells exhibit lower expression of Omp and JunD (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2M–N).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2M–N.

claim: The lower level of Omp suggests that the distinct cluster cells do not have the full characteristics of mature VSNs (mVSNs).
source: The lower level of Omp suggests that these cells do not have the full characteristics of mature VSNs (mVSNs), but they are also distinct from the immature VSNs (iVSNs) as they do not express higher levels of immature markers such as Gap43 and Stmn2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Omp expression data.

claim: The distinct cluster cells are distinct from the immature VSNs (iVSNs) as they do not express higher levels of immature markers such as Gap43 and Stmn2.
source: The lower level of Omp suggests that these cells do not have the full characteristics of mature VSNs (mVSNs), but they are also distinct from the immature VSNs (iVSNs) as they do not express higher levels of immature markers such as Gap43 and Stmn2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The lower expression of Ndua2, Ndua7, Cox6a1, and Cox7a2 suggests that the distinct cluster cells are less metabolically active than the canonical VSNs.
source: The lower expression of Ndua2, Ndua7, Cox6a1, and Cox7a2, which are involved in mitochondrial activities, suggest that these cells are less metabolically active than the canonical VSNs (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2O–R).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the expression data for mitochondrial genes.

claim: Pseudotime analysis found the distinct cluster to have similar pseudotime values as the mature V1R and V2R lineages.
source: To rule out the possibility that these cells were immature or senescent, we performed a pseudotime analysis on the neuronal lineage and found the cluster to have similar pseudotime values as the mature V1R and V2R linages (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: The distinct cluster cells are named as putative secretory VSNs (sVSNs).
source: Taken together, the gene expression profile suggests that this new class of neurons may not only sense environmental stimulus, but also may provide proteins to facilitate the clearing of the chemicals upon stimulation. We, therefore, name these cells as putative secretory VSNs (sVSNs).
evidence: This is a naming decision based on the gene expression profile.

claim: A distinct set of cells expressing the odorant receptors (ORs) comprise ~2.3% of the total neurons.
source: We also identify a distinct set of cells expressing the odorant receptors (ORs) that comprise ~2.3% of the total neurons (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the proportion of OR-expressing cells.

claim: A previous study has found the expression of ORs in neurons that display some typical molecular features of VSNs.
source: A previous study has found the expression of ORs in neurons that display some typical molecular features of VSNs, while another study detecting ORs in the VNO suggested the presence of non-canonical OSNs Lévai et al., 2006; Nakahara et al., 2016.
evidence: This statement references prior studies on OR expression in the VNO.

claim: OR expressing cells were shown to project to the AOB.
source: The OR expressing cells were shown to project to the AOB, but it was not clear how prevalent OR expression was in the VNO, nor whether the cells were VSNs or OSNs.
evidence: This statement references prior findings about OR-expressing cells.

claim: A majority of OR expressing cells lack V1R or V2R markers and form a cluster distinct from the V1R and V2R VSNs.
source: While some OR expressing cells cluster with the mature V1R or V2R neuronal lineages, a majority of these cells lacks V1R or V2R markers and forms a cluster distinct from the V1R and V2R VSNs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The majority of OR expressing cells express Gnal and Cnga2, which are the canonical markers of OSNs in the MOE.
source: These cells express Gnal and Cnga2, which are the canonical markers of OSNs in the MOE.
